description: Convert any video/image into a tiny size. 100% free & open-source. Available for Mac, Windows & Linux.

sources.entry: CompressO - Open-source tool for compressing videos and images to smaller sizes. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/codeforreal1/compressO) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: CompressO is a free, open-source desktop app for Linux, Windows and macOS that compresses videos and images to smaller file sizes.
summary.what_it_does: The app provides a desktop interface for shrinking video and image files. According to the README, the compression itself is done by third-party tools such as FFmpeg, pngquant, jpegoptim and gifski, using platform-specific standalone binaries. The app is built with Tauri (Rust) and a React frontend powered by Vite. The README says it works fully offline and makes no network requests except for built-in app updates. Installers are provided as .deb, AppImage, .dmg (Apple Silicon and Intel), and .msi, and Homebrew is available on macOS. The README also includes developer instructions for running the Tauri and Vite dev servers and producing a production build.
use_cases: compress large video files to share or upload
reduce video size without a command line
batch-free local media size reduction on Linux, Windows or macOS
how_to_run: Download an installer for your platform from the releases page (.deb, AppImage, .dmg, or .msi)
Development: install Rust and Node.js toolchains
Start the Tauri server: pnpm tauri:dev
Start the Vite server: pnpm vite:dev
notable: Runs entirely offline, with no network requests apart from built-in updates
Delegates compression to established open-source tools like FFmpeg and pngquant
Handles both video and image compression in one app
Homebrew cask install on macOS removes the quarantine attribute automatically
caveats: macOS builds are not notarized, so Gatekeeper warnings may require running xattr -cr or right-click Open (the Homebrew install avoids this)
Windows users may see a SmartScreen warning for the unsigned installer
Linux AppImage may crash or show a white screen, with workarounds via WEBKIT environment variables
